text: Mariam Kvrivishvili - We signed an updated version of the Free Trade Agreement with China, which will further strengthen and solidify trade and economic relations between the two countries (25.04.2026, 11:11)

The visit to the People’s Republic of China concluded with successful results, which will have a positive impact on the further development of economic ties between Georgia and China, - this was stated by the Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia, Mariam Kvrivishvili.

According to the Minister, during the visit, high-level meetings were held with representatives of China’s public and private sectors. Mariam Kvrivishvili placed special emphasis on the meeting held at China’s National Development and Reform Commission, during which the parties agreed to establish a Georgia-China dialogue mechanism to attract investment, which will facilitate the implementation of investments from China.

“Together with the Minister of Commerce, I signed the updated version of the free trade agreement, which will further strengthen and solidify trade and economic relations between the two countries. In addition, we made an extremely important decision to establish an intergovernmental format that will ensure the attraction of major investments, as well as support the involvement of Chinese companies in strategic projects,” said Mariam Kvrivishvili.

The Minister also highlighted the meeting held with the leadership of the Chinese airline China Eastern Airlines, at which a decision was made to launch direct flights between Shanghai and Tbilisi starting from July 15. As Mariam Kvrivishvili noted, the Shanghai route, as well as the Chinese tourism market in general, is strategic for Georgia, and direct air service will contribute both to an increase in tourist flows to the country and to the arrival of high-spending visitors.

“This decision will strengthen people-to-people relations, economic ties, and will give impetus to strengthening and diversifying our country’s tourism industry, as well as generating additional revenues in our country directly from the tourism industry,” said Mariam Kvrivishvili.

Within the framework of the visit, meetings were held with China’s largest energy and automobile manufacturing companies. As Mariam Kvrivishvili noted, the meetings discussed Georgia’s investment opportunities, which will help attract additional investment from China, develop local production, and strengthen the energy sector.
